The battery pack includes a plurality of battery cells enclosed within a housing, together with a fluid circulation path and a blower configured to circulate fluid through the pack. Gaps between adjacent battery cells form battery paths through which the fluid flows to regulate the temperature of the cells.

The fluid circulation system includes an inflow-side space and an outflow-side space. The inflow-side space distributes the circulating fluid to the inlets of the battery paths, while the outflow-side space collects the fluid discharged from the outlets of those paths. In addition, a separate circulation path extends along one or more inner surfaces of the housing.

The circulation system is configured so that the fluid flows more slowly in at least one of the inflow-side space and the outflow-side space than it does through the circulation path extending along the housing. This difference in flow velocity supports controlled fluid distribution and collection within the battery pack.

A battery pack includes a housing containing a plurality of battery cells and a blower configured to circulate a heat-transfer fluid, such as air, through the housing. Gaps are provided between adjacent cells so that the circulating fluid can flow along the cell surfaces and exchange heat with the cells. A distribution space positioned upstream of the cell gaps distributes the fluid among the gaps, while a collection space positioned downstream receives the fluid after it has passed between the cells.

The housing also defines a separate housing-side flow path extending along one or more inner surfaces of the housing. This path allows part of the blower-driven fluid to circulate around the cell assembly, apart from the flow passing directly through the intercell gaps. The distribution space, the collection space, the cell gaps, and the housing-side flow path may be connected to form an overall circulation circuit leading from the blower outlet back to the blower inlet.

The relative dimensions and flow resistances of the spaces and passages are selected so that the fluid velocity in at least one of the distribution space or the collection space is lower than the fluid velocity in the housing-side flow path. The lower-velocity region helps reduce pressure variations and promotes a more uniform supply of fluid to, or collection of fluid from, the individual gaps between cells. At the same time, the higher-velocity flow along the housing’s inner surfaces supports effective circulation around the battery assembly and limits stagnant regions.

By controlling the velocity relationship between these flow regions, the battery pack can improve the consistency of cooling or heating across the cells. More uniform cell temperatures can reduce localized thermal stress, limit temperature differences among cells, and support improved battery performance, durability, and safety. The arrangement also enables efficient thermal management using a compact blower-driven circulation system integrated within the battery-pack housing.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most frequently used words in the English language. Though it may seem insignificant, it helps speakers and writers point to something specific. We say “a book” when we mean any book, but “the book” when both speaker and listener know which book is being discussed.

This simple word creates clarity and connection. It can identify a unique object, such as “the sun,” emphasize importance, or guide the reader through a story. Without “the,” many English sentences would sound vague or incomplete. Its quiet but essential role shows that even the shortest words can have great power.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a battery pack that uses a blower and internal circulation paths to cool gaps between adjacent battery cells, including the inflow, outflow, and housing-side paths.
counterfactuals.output:
A battery pack includes a housing containing multiple battery cells arranged side by side with cooling gaps between adjacent cells. A blower circulates cooling air through the housing.

- **Inflow path:** Guides air from the blower’s discharge side to an inlet region communicating with the cell-to-cell gaps.
- **Inter-cell cooling paths:** Air passes through the gaps between adjacent battery cells, removing heat from the cell surfaces.
- **Outflow path:** Collects air exiting the inter-cell gaps and directs it toward the blower’s suction side.
- **Housing-side paths:** Additional circulation passages extend along one or more inner walls of the housing and connect the outflow and inflow regions. These paths allow air to return around the cell assembly rather than being exhausted outside the pack.

Together, the blower, inter-cell gaps, and housing-side paths form a substantially closed internal circulation loop, providing more uniform cell cooling while limiting exposure to outside air, moisture, and contaminants.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: What is the invention’s proposed battery-pack cooling architecture, and how do fluid velocities in the distribution spaces compare with the velocity along the case housing?
counterfactuals.output:
The invention integrates the cooling circuit into the battery-pack case. Coolant enters an inlet distribution space or header, is divided among multiple parallel cooling passages running along the case housing adjacent to the battery modules, and is collected in an outlet distribution space before leaving the pack.

Because the distribution spaces have a larger flow area and act as manifolds, coolant moves more slowly there than it does through the narrower passages along the case housing. This lower header velocity helps distribute the flow more uniformly among the parallel cooling paths.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
